question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Acids, Bases and Salts Practice Paper

questions.question_text: Which of the following compounds is the active constituent of bleaching powder?
options: CaO
Ca(ClO)2 or CaOCl2
CaCO3
Ca(OH)2
questions.correct_answer: Ca(ClO)2 or CaOCl2

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes key observations in Acids, Bases and Salts (Set 1)?
options: Core process in Acids, Bases and Salts obeys conservation laws and standard reaction conditions.
Process in Acids, Bases and Salts violates mass conservation.
No physical or chemical state change occurs during the reaction.
Products have higher total mass than initial reactants.
questions.correct_answer: Core process in Acids, Bases and Salts obeys conservation laws and standard reaction conditions.

questions.question_text: What physical state symbol or indicator color change is associated with Acids, Bases and Salts (Set 1)?
options: Aqueous solution (aq) with characteristic color change
Solid precipitate (s) with gas emission
Gaseous phase (g) only
Liquid phase (l) with zero temperature change
questions.correct_answer: Aqueous solution (aq) with characteristic color change

questions.question_text: Identify the correct SI unit or mathematical relationship relevant to Acids, Bases and Salts (Set 1).
options: Standard NCERT Formula & Unit
Dimensionless Ratio x 100
Inverse Square Exponential
Absolute Constant Zero
questions.correct_answer: Standard NCERT Formula & Unit

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Fundamental processes in Acids, Bases and Salts strictly follow thermodynamic and chemical principles.
Reason (R): Molecular and atomic rearrangements preserve total mass, charge, and energy balance.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.correct_answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.question_text: Why does tooth decay start when the pH of the mouth falls below 5.5?
options: Option A
Option B
Option C
Option D
questions.correct_answer: Tooth enamel (calcium hydroxyapatite) begins to corrode when mouth pH falls below 5.5 due to acid production by bacteria digesting food particles.

questions.question_text: Explain the chlor-alkali process and list the three chemical products generated along with their respective points of formation.
options: Option A
Option B
Option C
Option D
questions.correct_answer: Passage of electricity through aqueous sodium chloride (brine) decomposes it into Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH near cathode), Chlorine gas (Cl2 at anode), and Hydrogen gas (H2 at cathode).
